reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the output is consistent with that: no redline (rendered text is identical to the originals) and no counterparty comment, which is the correct output for a compliant finding.

The cited text supports compliance on the rule's material terms: Section 14 (p0079) presupposes and operationalises a Client 'election to terminate this Agreement' unqualified by breach, cause or consent, with the effective date running to the last day of the month following notice (~30–60 days), and no early-termination fee, penalty or clawback appears anywhere in the cited paragraphs.

Vendor side is directionally correct — TrueLink's only exits are for-cause termination of Sections 2/3 on Client breach or a System/Credit Repository default, plus symmetrical 30-day non-renewal at end of term; there is no mid-term Vendor convenience right, so the walk-away triggers are not engaged.
The 1-year initial term auto-renewing in successive one-year periods means the 'multi-year term with no Customer convenience right' walk-away test does not apply.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is adequately reconciled: the clause expresses the right functionally rather than using the label 'convenience' (the only use of that word is the captions boilerplate). This is a phrasing variant, not a substantive gap, so the heuristic miss does not overturn the substance.

Sub-elements short of the preferred wording (no express pro-rata prepaid-fee refund — moot given monthly arrears invoicing under Section 5a; the 30-day non-renewal notice; the 'Subject to Section 4' blank minimum-commitment period and the Section 13 mis-cross-reference to Section 12) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined, per the playbook's classification semantics. Flagging these would have been over-flagging of a clause that already benefits us.
